subject.title: fix(codex): reject hex/exponent computer wait duration strings

question: Should Codex watchdog budgeting continue to recognize plain decimal duration strings, or should it accept only finite JSON numbers to match the canonical computer-tool input contract?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but choosing which previously coerced string forms remain supported is an upgrade-sensitive compatibility decision not established by the upstream transport or current user documentation.

options.title: Numbers only
options.body: Accept finite non-negative JSON numbers, including fractions, and treat every string duration as invalid in both execution and watchdog budgeting.

options.title: Keep decimal strings
options.body: Retain plain decimal integer strings as compatibility input while rejecting hexadecimal, exponent, and fractional strings, with explicit contract tests and documentation.

options.title: Preserve coercion
options.body: Keep the current JavaScript coercion behavior and close this PR if maintainers consider all existing string forms part of the supported contract.

recommendation.title: Numbers only
recommendation.body: Accept finite non-negative JSON numbers, including fractions, and treat every string duration as invalid in both execution and watchdog budgeting.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across the Codex app-server timeout path and adjacent computer-tool surface.
